microarchitecture_summary.implementation_style: Single-module synchronous RTL with one 8-bit registered counter and one combinational compare for PWM decode.
microarchitecture_summary.control_strategy: On each rising edge of clk, synchronous active-low reset clears the counter to 0; otherwise enable gates whether the counter holds, increments, or wraps to 0 at the inclusive period terminal count.
microarchitecture_summary.state_strategy: The only state element is the 8-bit counter register driving counter_value; duty_cycle and period are used directly as unsigned inputs with no shadow registers or hidden state.
microarchitecture_summary.output_strategy: counter_value directly reflects the registered counter; pwm_out is a purely combinational function of counter_value < duty_cycle.

fsm_intent.description: No explicit FSM is implied or required. Counter hold/increment/wrap behavior is implemented with simple conditional next-state logic.

sequencing_notes: Sample behavior on the rising edge of clk only.
If reset_n is low on a clock edge, synchronously clear counter state to 8'h00.
If reset_n is high and enable is low, hold the counter value.
If reset_n is high and enable is high, wrap to 0 when the current counter equals period; otherwise increment by 1.
If period is 0, enabled operation keeps the counter at 0.
pwm_out is not registered and updates combinationally from the current counter_value and duty_cycle.
timing_notes: Target timing intent aligns to the declared 50 MHz / 20 ns clock domain.
reset_n is synchronous, so no asynchronous reset timing arc is implied.
The pwm_out compare path is a simple 8-bit unsigned magnitude comparison from the registered counter and input duty_cycle.
No multicycle, CDC, or handshake timing assumptions are implied by the spec.
ownership_notes: This module owns the only state element required by the specification.
This module owns the counter wrap/hold/increment behavior and PWM decode.
No subordinate modules, memories, or hidden interfaces are implied.
Interfaces remain exactly as defined in digital_spec_json.
consistency_notes: Interfaces remain exactly as defined in digital_spec_json.
